issues.body:
When the raw-string terminator or `*/` is not found, both branches set `end = len(content)` and mask the remainder of the file. Confirmed at PR head:

  `let s = r#"oops;\n#[cfg(feature = "live")]\n` -> `_extract_cfg_expressions()` returns `[]`
  `/* oops\n#[cfg(feature = "live")]\n`          -> `[]`

That is a silent erasure in the demotion direction, which is the one thing classify_leg's docstring promises cannot happen ("A detector bug can only keep a full leg; it can never silently demote a sensitive leg"). Severity is nit rather than major because both inputs are non-compiling Rust — the tree this scans is built by cargo on the same PR, so the state is not reachable in practice, and it is strictly better than the pre-PR regex which handled neither construct at all. Raising it only so the residual is recorded rather than discovered later.
issues.fix_hint: In the raw-string and block-comment branches, when the terminator is not found, treat the construct as NOT a literal/comment: leave the span unmasked and advance `i += 1` instead of masking to EOF. A spurious extra cfg only retains a leg (fail-closed), which matches the documented invariant. Two extra cases in TestCfgExtraction (the two repros above, asserting `['feature = "live"']`) would pin it.
issues.title: Unterminated raw string or block comment masks to EOF, dropping every later cfg (fail-open direction)

issues.body: Measured on this checkout: sanitizing all 1324 crates/**/*.rs files (32.8 MB) takes 7.6 s with the new scanner vs 1.1 s with the pre-PR regexes; a full classify over the 169 real fragment legs goes 4.1 s -> 15.9 s (each leg re-reads and re-sanitizes its crate, so files under multi-leg crates are re-scanned once per leg). 16 s is fine for a CI ratchet step, so this is informational, not a defect — noting it because the cost scales with both the crate tree and the leg count, and both grow.
issues.fix_hint: If it ever becomes noticeable, memoize the sanitized text (or the extracted expression list) per file path within a single process run — e.g. a dict keyed by resolved path in _classify_feature_in_src_files / _classify_feature_in_test_files, or an lru_cache on a small `_cfg_exprs_for_file(path)` helper. No behavioural change; the detector is read-only over a fixed tree for the duration of a run.
issues.title: Per-character Python scan is ~4x slower on the classify/enforce path

verdict.summary:
Round 4 replaces the whack-a-mole regex masking with a real left-to-right lexer, which resolves the round-3 major and all three minors. Everything below was re-verified independently, not taken on trust.

RESOLVED (major, phantom raw-string opener / fail-open): _sanitize_for_cfg_scan is now a single-pass scanner over {line comment, nested block comment, raw string with N hashes, b/c-prefixed and ordinary string, char literal} that masks in place preserving length and CR/LF. All three round-3 repros are fixed at PR head: `let m = "mode r";`, `let m = "w/r";` and `#[cfg(feature = "vector-r")]` followed by a second cfg now each extract the correct expressions (previously [] , [] , and one mangled expr). Tree-wide check over 1324 crates/**/*.rs files: 3822 line-anchored cfg attributes survive sanitization, 0 files lose any, 0 extraction exceptions, and len(safe)==len(content) holds everywhere. Behaviour-preservation: I ran classify_leg over all 169 real fragment legs under BOTH the pre-PR (HEAD~1) and the new sanitizer — 152/169 sensitive under both, 0 legs changed classification, cmd_enforce exits 0 with 0 violations. Adversarial probes all correct: lifetimes/labels vs char literals, `'"'`, raw idents `r#type`, nested `/* /* */ */`, b""/c""/cr#"" decoys, CRLF, `a / *p`.

RESOLVED (minor, vacuous fixture): the new test_extract_single_cfg fixture returns the mangled `['feature = "vector-r")]\nfn a() {}...']` under the pre-PR regex and the correct two exprs under the new code — genuinely red-on-old. Same for test_ordinary_literal_trailing_r_does_not_open_raw_string and test_nested_block_comment_cfg_is_masked. Suite: 56 tests OK.

RESOLVED (minor, doc): TestMutationFailOpen::test_mutation_check_divergence exists (lines 574/602); the arrow rationale checks out against crates/sparq-py/src/lib.rs:46; 58 -> 52 = 58 - 6 is now consistent; 0 legs declare a tier, so 0 -> 0 is accurate.

Only two nits remain; nothing blocking.
